name: Sara Dunjo
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.source_named: Retired glottocode: Sara Dunjo [koj] merged into Sara Kaba Naa [kwv] (ISO CR 2014-030); Glottolog lists no references.

new_statements.quote: 1.3 Tone. Like the Sara Languages, Na has three level tones: high, mid and low: ká 'so that, for', kō 'already', ɓà 'rainy season'. Tone-bearing phonemes are vowels and sonorant consonants when they are in final position. When a morpheme contains a sequence of identical vowels with distinct tones, or when a sonorant consonant closes a syllable, complex tones occur [...] Of the nine possible combinations, Mid-Low is not found. High-Low, which is very rare in the Sara languages with native morphemes, is common in Na, and is frequently used in verb conjugations.

new_statements.rule_in_words: Na (incl. its Dunje/Dunjo dialect area around Kyabé) is described as a three-level register tone language (H, M, L, with contours on VV sequences and coda sonorants); the description contains no statement of any kind about word stress or accent, so no stress position can be extracted. Only incidental prominence-adjacent remark: morpheme-final vowels of lexical morphemes are phonetically longer, vowel length not phonemic (§1.2).
new_statements.exceptions: None regarding stress; tonal alternations (H > HL phrase-finally, LL > LH before kō, M > MH before clause marker nē) described in §1.4.
new_statements.domain_note: Statement concerns lexical tone on morphemes/words; nothing on word- or phrase-level stress. Intro was reviewed by Jim Roberts (SIL / Univ. N'Djamena).
new_statements.identity_note: sara1320 'Sara Dunjo' [koj] is a Glottolog bookkeeping languoid: ISO 639-3 CR 2014-030 merged koj into Sara Kaba Náà [kwv] (Glottolog sara1321), where 'Dunje' is listed as a dialect alongside Banga, Na and Tie. All accessible description is of Na (Sara Kaba Na) as spoken around Kyabé, principal consultant Kodé Koutou; Keegan notes (fn. 3, p. ix) that little dialectal variation is included, and the Dunjo are mentioned only as an ethnic group in a dictionary example (s.v. ndājó). Any catalog entry should be filed under sara1321 / kwv, not under the retired code.
